- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.2) and forecast is below recent low, adjust upward by 1–2% to capture bullish momentum.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.2) and forecast is above recent high, reduce by 1–2% to avoid overcorrection.  
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% above recent peak) should be capped at +5% of prior peak to prevent overbought bias.  
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is consistently 2–3% above true outcome over 5+ days, reduce by 0.5–1% per day until convergence.  
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is volatile (±0.3+ in last 5 days), reduce forecast volatility by 10–20% to avoid overfitting to noise.  
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% for 3 consecutive days, assume sentiment is bullish and adjust next forecast up by 1–1.5% to align with momentum.
